high.title: Iran Closes Strait of Hormuz Again and Scares Markets; Oil and Ibovespa in Dollars Rise Today (20)
high.summary: Markets operate with caution on Monday (20) amid rising tensions in the Middle East, while oil prices advance. The movement follows a weekend marked by new episodes of instability that reduced expectations for progress in peace negotiations between the US and Iran before the ceasefire deadline. On Sunday, President Trump stated that the US Navy intercepted and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. This action came after Iran refused to participate in a new round of negotiations scheduled in Pakistan. The episode represents an escalation in regional tensions. On Sunday, Tehran allegedly fired at commercial vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the most important passages for global oil flow. Since last week, the US has maintained a naval blockade. This geopolitical tension directly impacts oil prices and creates risk-off sentiment affecting emerging market currencies like the BRL. Brazilian markets show resilience with Ibovespa gains in dollar terms, but sustained tensions could pressure the Real and increase volatility in Brazilian assets.

high.title: IPCA, IGP-10: What to Expect from Brazilian Economy Amid Middle East Conflict Escalation
high.summary: The IGP-10 and Focus Bulletin this week reflected what is no longer news: economic deterioration in view of the Middle East conflict. The war escalation raised oil and derivatives prices, bringing upward revisions to inflation projections. IGP-10 on Wednesday (15) registered a 2.94% increase in April, contrasting with the 0.24% drop in March. Meanwhile, estimates for other indicators are being revised. This week, the Focus Bulletin followed this worsening market sentiment, with IPCA expectations for 2026 at 4.71% and maintaining a high interest rate scenario with Selic at 12.50% for the year. Beyond oil prices, Middle East war developments impact the entire production chain comprehensively - affecting fuel costs, freight transport, supermarket logistics, and ultimately food prices, also reaching fertilizers and raising agricultural production costs. This creates significant challenges for Brazilian monetary policy and could pressure the BCB to maintain higher rates longer than previously anticipated.

medium.title: Real Time: Ibovespa Operates with Low Liquidity
medium.summary: Ibovespa opens the week at a slower pace due to the holiday bridge in Brazil, which tends to reduce trading volume throughout the session. Despite this, the market continues to function normally and may react to specific flow movements. The domestic highlight is the Focus Report updating inflation and interest rate projections, while abroad Japan releases its trade balance. Bitcoin trades around $75,000 with slight declines.

medium.title: B3 Extends Hours and Now Trades Crypto and Gold Until 8 PM
medium.summary: Starting Monday (20), B3 operates with extended hours for Bitcoin (BIT), Ethereum (ETR), Solana (SOL) and gold (GLD) futures contracts. These assets can now be traded from 9 AM to 8 PM, expanding the trading window to 11 continuous hours. The extension occurs amid growing demand for exposure to crypto assets and precious metals within regulated environments, plus investors seeking greater flexibility to adjust positions outside traditional market hours.

medium.title: Bradesco (BBDC4) Buys Remaining Stake from Banco BV in Tivio Capital
medium.summary: Bradesco announced Monday (20) it completed the acquisition of Tivio Capital by purchasing Banco BV's stake in the asset manager, aiming to expand alternative product offerings to clients. Tivio was born in 2023 when Bradesco bought 51% control of BV Asset, created in 1999. The asset manager will continue operating independently with its own governance and investment autonomy. This consolidates Bradesco's strategic push into alternative investments, following a global trend toward more sophisticated financial products.

medium.title: Ana Paula, Milena, Juliano Floss: Who Will Profit in Conservative Fixed Income with Selic at 14.75% with BBB 26's R$5.4 Million Prize?
medium.summary: BBB 26 finalists compete for an unprecedented R$5.44 million prize. When contestants entered the house in January, Selic was at 15% annually, but BCB cut it to 14.75% last month. Despite the rate cut, conservative fixed income remains the most attractive asset class currently, offering solid returns for the potential winner's investment strategy.
